results.evidence: The button calls `moveToDraft`, which runs `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., { status: 'draft' })`. `isReadOnly` is `broadcast.status !== 'draft'`, so the wizard becomes editable. But the patch leaves the schedules in place and adds no scheduler guard, so whether the send stops while it is a draft depends on unseen backend code.

The gate is `broadcast?.status === 'active' && !latestBatchJob`. It never checks for a pending schedule. An active broadcast with no batch job and no schedule, or a completed one-time schedule, would still show the button. It can also show before `batchJobs` has loaded.

`for (const existing of values.broadcast?.schedules ?? []) { await hogFlowsSchedulesDestroy(...) }` runs before either the immediate batch job or `hogFlowsSchedulesCreate`. Every old schedule is deleted and a single new one is created. The immediate path leaves none.

`activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` runs before the schedule destroy and create. An interruption part-way, such as a page close, leaves the broadcast live with none or a partial schedule. The catch-block revert to draft does not run if the tab dies.
The only guards are `status === 'active'` and `!latestBatchJob`. There is no check for in-progress run status, unknown run history, multiple schedules or a modified workflow shape.
The button's `onClick={() => moveToDraft()}` acts immediately. There is no confirmation dialog.
`moveToDraft` only patches the status and shows 'Broadcast moved to draft'. It never cancels a batch job and has no warning or partial-failure messaging.
The patch touches only the two frontend files. There is no scheduler or backend change that re-checks the status before creating a run.
Existing schedules are destroyed, and the new one is built from only `rrule`, `starts_at` and `timezone`. Any variables on the old schedule are dropped.

result:
A live scheduled broadcast can now be moved back to draft, and launching now replaces any existing schedule with a fresh one. I haven't run the type check, lint or tests, and I didn't add a test.

- **Move to draft:** the Broadcasts summary page has a new "Move to draft" button, in `BroadcastSummary.tsx`. It shows only when the broadcast is active and hasn't sent yet. It sets the broadcast's status to `draft` and drops you into the wizard's review step to edit and relaunch. Its handler is a new `moveToDraft` action in `broadcastWizardLogic.ts`, which also adds a `movingToDraft` loading flag for the button.
- **Relaunch fix:** `launchBroadcast` in `broadcastWizardLogic.ts` now deletes every existing schedule on the broadcast before creating the new one (or the immediate send). Because the API can't resume a schedule that an audience edit paused, the paused schedule is now deleted and replaced with a new, active one. This also stops an old schedule from firing again after a "send now" relaunch.

I left the old schedules in place when a broadcast moves to draft. That keeps the wizard prefilled with its previous send time, and the relaunch replaces them anyway.

The button hides once a broadcast has any batch job, so a broadcast that has started sending can't be pulled back.
